column1: # Classified differences between GNU Make 4.4.1 and the Make front end over the
# vendored kati corpus.  Regenerate the case rows with
# `scripts/check-make-conformance.sh --update`; the class and family columns are
# a judgement and are edited by hand.
# class    defect     a real difference from GNU Make that Make mode must fix
#          recorded   the corpus itself annotates the case as not matching Make
#                     (`# TODO` at the head of the file, as run_test.go reads it)
#          extension  the case exercises a kati-only feature, so GNU Make cannot
#                     be the oracle; the corpus fakes Make's side of it
#          artefact   the difference is caused by the corpus or the harness
# digest   FNV-1a over both observations.  A recorded difference that changes
#          shape fails the run and has to be reclassified.
# family   record: name and the reason that family exists.
# case     record: id, class, `+`-joined families, digest.

column3: += onto a variable that is defined but empty inserts a separator space. GNU Make appends without one. Present in the C++ original (SimpleVar::AppendVar) and in the Rust port, so it is inherited rather than introduced.
the two tools schedule an order-only prerequisite at different points, so the recipe echoes interleave differently.
the corpus annotates the case with a leading # TODO, which is how the vendored harness recorded that kati does not match GNU Make here.
the case gates its expectation on $(filter 4.2%,$(MAKE_VERSION)), so moving the oracle off the vendored harness's 4.2.1 pin changes which branch GNU Make takes.
kati names the goal rather than the rule that actually wanted the missing prerequisite.
GNU Make brackets a -C build with Entering directory / Leaving directory; kati prints neither.
GNU Make 4.0+ names the makefile line inside *** [Makefile:N: target] Error N; kati writes only the target.
the makefile evaluates to something else: a different value, a different rule chosen, or a directive kati does not implement.
GNU Make exits 2 when it abandons a build; kati exits 1. The status is documented and scripts branch on it.
the case drives --use_find_emulator, kati's in-process replacement for find(1), which is a deliberate departure from what a recipe would do.
GNU Make prefixes a diagnostic that carries no makefile location with its own name and a colon; kati prints it bare.
the Rust port renders io::Error with its "(os error N)" suffix, which GNU Make does not print.
the case exercises a feature GNU Make does not have, so the corpus writes Make's side of the comparison by hand and only kati's side is evidence.
the diagnostic says the same thing in different words from GNU Make's.
kati quotes names as `x' , the GNU Make 3.8x style. 4.4.1 quotes 'x'.
kati captures a recipe's combined output and writes it to its own stdout; GNU Make lets the recipe inherit both descriptors, so a recipe's stderr stays on stderr.
GNU Make 4.x says "recipe" where 3.8x said "commands"; kati kept the older wording.
GNU Make appends "  Stop." to the fatal diagnostic it dies on; kati prints the diagnostic alone.
